title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Alsace and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Alsace labels show the grape, the producer, and sometimes a Grand Cru, a commune, VT or SGN. Crémant d'Alsace marks traditional method sparkling wine, France's most produced crémant. The flûte bottle is required for still wines. A sweetness indicator often appears on the back.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Alsace wines suit its rich food: choucroute garnie, sauerkraut with sausages, goes with Riesling or Pinot Gris; Munster cheese with Gewürztraminer; tarte flambée, a thin bacon and onion tart, with Pinot Blanc or Riesling; foie gras with VT. They also suit Asian food, especially Gewürztraminer and off-dry Pinot Gris.

steps.prompt: Match each dish to an Alsace wine.
steps.explanation: Alsace wines match its local food.

steps.body: Crémant d'Alsace, often made from Pinot Blanc, Auxerrois and Riesling, is one of France's best-value sparkling wines.

steps.prompt: Alsace still wines must be sold in the tall flûte bottle.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show grape, producer and sometimes Grand Cru
Alsace wines suit choucroute, Munster and tarte flambée
Crémant d'Alsace is great-value sparkling wine
